ust10y.credit: Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates (10 Yr), accessed 2026-11-10

defaults.discount_rate_text: US 10-year Treasury 4.88% on 9 November 2026 + 5 pp equity risk premium (assumption)

definitions.debt_rule:
1. DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount when reported (the company's own total).
    2. Else noncurrent debt + current debt, where current debt is DebtCurrent when reported, otherwise current
       maturities plus short-term borrowings (or commercial paper); short-term borrowings equal to the current
       maturities are the same line and are counted once. For an issuer that tags current maturities only by
       segment (listed by hand: Caterpillar), the current maturities come from its debt maturity schedule.
    3. Else LongTermDebt (including current maturities) plus short-term borrowings.
    4. Else the current parts alone (DebtCurrent, or current maturities plus short-term borrowings).
    5. With no debt tag at all, 0 ("no debt tags in the 10-K"). A blocked (conflicting) tag is never 0.

    The second value maps "noncurrent" and "current" to True when that maturity's debt tag includes capital or
    finance leases (LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations[Current]); None means unknown (combined total).
definitions.ebitda: operating income (lab.fundamentals) + D&A; without an operating income tag, pre-tax income + interest expense + D&A (labelled in the formula)
definitions.ev_definition: market cap + debt + finance leases + non-controlling interest − cash − short-term investments; operating leases are not added because US GAAP EBITDA is already after rent
definitions.leverage: net debt = debt + finance leases not inside debt - cash - short-term investments (operating leases left out); net debt / EBITDA; EBITDA / interest, where interest is gross interest expense, else net interest expense, else cash interest paid (named in the formula)
definitions.history: up to 5 lined-up fiscal years (each ends the day before the next starts), oldest first, same definitions; each year's value is its latest 10-K disclosure

notes: Enterprise value adds debt, finance leases and non-controlling interest to the market value of equity and subtracts cash and short-term investments. Operating leases are shown but not added: under US GAAP, EBITDA is already after rent.

Debt follows one rule for every company (the company's own combined total when reported, otherwise noncurrent plus current debt); some issuers report debt only by segment, so totals can be understated. Every component links to its filing.

The DCF is a two-stage model on unlevered free cash flow (cash from operations − capex + after-tax interest): growth for five years, fading to terminal growth by year ten. Defaults are stated; change them.
Banks, brokers and insurers (SIC 6000–6799) get no EV bridge, EBITDA or DCF: deposits and trading liabilities make these measures meaningless.
Market values are not shown: the prices are private until publication is confirmed.
Hypothetical model on stated assumptions; not investment advice; no price targets.
